text:
jamie: Quick heads-up — I repro'd a perf regression on long-context workloads. Pattern: KV slab "wobble" (frequent small frees/allocs) makes the batch-merge policy split batches too often, causing head-of-line blocking and latency tails.

jamie: Perf snapshot (sample-based):
```
# perf top -p 12345
  23.4%  runtime  [kernel.kallsyms]  kv_slab_alloc+0x4f
  19.1%  runtime  [kernel.kallsyms]  kv_slab_free+0x3a
  11.8%  runtime  libc.so.6     memcpy+0x1a
   9.7%  runtime  libthread.so   spin_lock+0x20
```

jamie: pprof (server) shows spikes in allocator/meta-path around batch merge points. Flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/2789 (short-lived spikes coincident with batch merges).

nata: ugh. repro steps? can we run a tiny harness?

jamie: Minimal repro I used (bash):
```bash
# spawn many long ctx requests with varying prefix lengths to exercise reuse + fragmentation
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  ./stress-client --model=redwood-std --seq=8192 --prefix-len=$((RANDOM%4096)) &
done
```
It only reproduces under continuous-batching enabled + merge_policy=aggressive.

leo: I pulled a heap profile. The interesting bit is not raw bytes but slot churn — free/alloc rate jumps at the same time the batch merge code calls split(). Looks like the merge path touches slab metadata per-slot which is not amortized.

leo: snippet from heap sample:
```
# top allocation stacks
kv_slot_meta_alloc
kv_slab_lock
contbatch_merge_split
contbatch_headblock_wait
```

sara: two quick mitigation ideas: bias merge policy to prefer "append-only" merges (if most slots contiguous) and add a fast-path for small-batch merge that doesn't touch per-slot metadata. Also consider throttling merges when slab_free_rate > X to avoid thrashing.

jamie: Agree. I sketched a cheap heuristic: if recent_free_rate > 200 ops/s and avg_slot_occupancy < 0.2 then temporarily set merge_threshold_ms += 20 and cap splits_per_epoch to 2.

nata: can we feature-flag that? want to run A/B to ensure we don't regress throughput.

jamie: Yes flag + runtime knob. Plan: 1) add metric kv_free_rate, slot_occupancy, split_count; 2) implement throttling heuristic behind flag; 3) run bench-suite (longctx 8k, 16k) on dedicate CI.

leo: Also important: check kernel selection interactions — on A100 we have different memcpy/kernels so the cost profile changes. Might be worth disabling aggressive merging only on platforms where kv_slab_lock contention is dominant.

sara: small note — there is a subtle correctness window: delaying splits means merges can grow and increase latency for large single requests. We'll need guardrails (max_merge_size).

jamie: Agreed. Proposed defaults: max_merge_size = 256k, splits_per_epoch = 2, emergency_backoff if free_rate > 500/s. I'll prototype.

ci-bot: triggered job: perf/kv-wobble/2789456123, status: queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:

nata: TL;DR action items?

jamie: Action list:
- jamie: prototype throttling heuristic + flag, push PR to feature/kv-wobble.
- leo: run flamegraph comparison across GPU types and collect memcpy/kernel profiles.
- sara: write canary config for dedicated cluster with guardrails.
- nata: run bench matrix and capture latency p99/p999.

sara: tagging this P1 for short-term mitigation, P2 for long-term redesign of per-slot meta touching in merge path.

leo: one extra note — if we can reduce metadata writes in contbatch_merge_split by coalescing updates, that might be the clean fix. I can try a patch after initial experiments.

jamie: ok I'll open the PR and link the perf traces. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
